properties.service_contract: Creates a new user account from the submitted credentials and profile details, hashing the password with a freshly generated salt and enabling the account immediately. The flow rejects empty credentials and duplicate usernames, and binds any roles submitted with the registration to the new account.

Authenticates a visitor against the user store with username and password, keeps the signed-in identity across visits, signs the subject out again, and reports the current authentication status of the request.
Lists all user accounts together with the roles bound to each account, for the back-office user management screen.
Updates an account's profile contact details and rebinds the roles assigned to that account.
Enables or disables a user account; an account that is disabled is refused at sign-in.
Resets an account's password to a fixed default value, re-salting the stored credential so the new password is recorded.
Lists the role records together with the permissions and menus each role carries, for the back-office role management screen.
Creates a new role or updates an existing role record, and rebinds the role's permission set to the submitted permissions.
Enables or disables a role.
Publishes the permission records the role editor draws on, each naming a protected management surface.
Rebinds a role's menu set, replacing the previous assignments with the submitted menu identifiers.
Serves the navigation menu tree for the currently signed-in user and the menu set belonging to a role, used to build the back-office navigation.
Lists the book catalog either in full or filtered to the books of a chosen category, newest records first.
Finds books whose title or author matches a submitted keyword and returns them newest first.
Creates or updates a book record carrying title, author, publication date, press, abstract, cover reference and category.
Removes a book record by its identifier.
Receives an uploaded cover image, stores it under the workspace image folder under a randomized file name, and returns the file reference used to display it.
Serves a stored cover image file back to the browser for inline display.
Saves a jotter article with its title, markdown source, rendered html, abstract, cover reference and date.
Removes a jotter article by its identifier.
Lists jotter articles newest first in pages and serves a single article by its identifier for reading.
Authenticate an existing account holder and start their session. Deals in credentials, login, sign-in, single sign-on and session start.
Create a new account from user-supplied details and verify it. Deals in registration, sign-up, account creation and verification.
Let a locked-out account holder prove identity without a password and set a new one. Deals in forgotten passwords, reset tokens and links, security questions and password change.

properties.description: The White Jotter SPA exposes a same-origin authentication and self-registration surface via client-side routes /login, /register, and /authentication, reconfirmed by repeated references in the JS bundle. Because the origin is served over cleartext HTTP, credential submission to these routes is exposed to network interception unless HTTPS is enforced. Registration may permit unauthenticated account creation, and the login/register flows are prime targets for credential stuffing and account enumeration. The actual server-side authentication flow — session issuance, token handling, or password reset — is still not witnessed; only the client-side route map is confirmed.

properties.description: Vue single-page application served as the root HTML shell for the White Jotter service. The root page is a webpack-built SPA, and the application is identifiable as a Spring Boot/Vue blog project, which hints at known admin/content-management API routes for later enumeration. The client-side route map includes /login, /register, /authentication, /admin, /admin/dashboard, /admin/content/editor, /api, /menu, /index, /jotter, /jotter/article, /library, and /home; these are client-side routes, not confirmed server-rendered pages, and their presence does not enforce access control. The root response remains unhardened — no Content-Security-Policy, no X-Frame-Options, no X-Content-Type-Options, no Strict-Transport-Security — so browser-enforced protections against XSS payload loading, clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and cleartext downgrade are absent. The Server: nginx/1.30.1 header discloses the exact web server version, enabling precise stack fingerprinting.
